title: Miller Indices & Crystal Defects
subtitle: Miller indices are the coordinate system of crystals — how we name planes and directions. Crystal defects are the imperfections that make materials interesting (and sometimes weak). Both are high-yield exam topics.
learningOutcome: Miller indices are the coordinate system of crystals — how we name planes and directions. Crystal defects are the imperfections that make materials interesting (and sometimes weak). Both are high-yield exam topics.

content.text: The numerical system used to describe the points, planes and directions in a crystal are called crystallographic indices. The indices l, m, and n are called Miller indices.
6-Step procedure to find Miller indices of a plane:

items: • Set up a right-handed x-y-z coordinate system. If the plane passes through the origin, take a new origin at an adjacent corner.
• Find where the plane intersects each axis (in units of a, b, c). If parallel to an axis, intercept = ∞.
• Multiply by the lowest common factor to get the smallest integers.
• Enclose in parentheses (hkl) — no commas. Negative values get a bar over the number.
• For a family of equivalent planes, use curly braces {hkl}.

content.caption: Key Crystallographic Planes in a Cubic Cell

content.text: Family of planes {hkl} — all crystallographically equivalent planes. {100} includes: (100), (010), (001), (1̄00), (01̄0), (001̄) — the six faces of a cube. Family of directions <uvw> — all equivalent directions. <110> includes: [110],[101],[011],[1̄10],[1̄01],[01̄1],[11̄0],[101̄],[011̄] — 12 directions Planar density = number of atoms centred on plane / area of plane in unit cell Linear density = number of atoms centred on direction / length of direction

⚠ Common Mistake Planes use ( ) parentheses. Directions use [ ] square brackets. Families of planes use { } curly braces. Families of directions use < > angle brackets. Mixing these up costs marks. Also — a negative intercept is written as a bar OVER the number, not as a minus sign before it. You cannot write (-1,0,0); you write (1̄00).

content.text: A crystalline defect is the lattice irregularity having one or more of its dimensions on the order of an atomic diameter. The imperfection or irregularity of the geometrical arrangement of atoms in a crystalline solid is called a crystalline defect.

items: Interruption in the regularity of a crystal lattice at a point
Interruption in the regularity of a crystal lattice along a line
Interruption in the regularity over an area
Interruption in the regularity in some volume

content.text: N = total number of atomic sites (atoms/m³) · Q v = energy required for vacancy formation (eV) · k = Boltzmann's constant = 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J/(atom·K) or 8.62 × 10⁻⁵ eV/atom·K · T = temperature in Kelvin Example: Find equilibrium vacancies for copper at 1000°C T = 1273 K, Q v = 0.9 eV/atom, atomic weight = 63.5 g/mol, density = 8.4 g/cm³ N = (density × N A ) / atomic weight = (8.4 × 6.02×10²³) / 63.5 = 7.96 × 10²² atoms/cm³ N v = 7.96×10²² × e^(−0.9/8.62×10⁻⁵×1273) = 2.2 × 10¹⁸ vacancies/cm³

content.text: Two dislocations can interact to form a third if the reaction LOWERS energy. Criterion: |b₃|² < |b₁|² + |b₂|² (energy of resultant < energy of reactants) Example: Can [123] and [2 0 1] interact? b₃ = [123] + [201] = [3 2 4] |b₁|² = 1²+2²+3² = 14 · |b₂|² = 2²+0²+1² = 5 · |b₁|²+|b₂|² = 19 |b₃|² = 3²+2²+4² = 9+4+16 = 29 Since 29 > 19, interaction is NOT possible (would increase energy). Example: Can [1̄35] and [134] interact? b₃ = [-1+1, 3+3, 5+4] = [0 6 9] — check: 0+36+81=117 > (1+9+25)+(1+9+16)=61 → NOT possible.

Dislocation interaction questions have appeared in 2011, 2015, 2019 and 2021 papers. Always: (1) add the Burgers vectors to get b₃; (2) calculate |b|² for each; (3) compare sum of reactants to product. If product energy > sum of reactants → NOT possible. State what reaction IS possible if asked.
